newsitem.title: USA: BP says most of its Gulf oil/gas output shut in.
newsitem.headline: BP says most of its Gulf oil/gas output shut in.

text.p: BP Oil said most of its oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico was shut in Friday after Hurricane Danny passed through, but it expected to restore output by Saturday if conditions permit.

Three of four oil and gas fields operated by BP in the Gulf were shut in, representing 45,000 barrels per day of crude oil and 50 million cubic feet a day of natural gas, said Hugh Depland, a spokesman for BP.
Together with other BP equity oil and gas shut in on fields operated by other companies, the bulk of BP's output in the area was shut in on Friday, Depland said.

But production at the three affected fields -- Pompano in Viosca Knoll block 989, Amberjack in Mississippi Canyon 109 and Ewing Bank 826 -- are expected to be back by Saturday, after the heavy rains pass and assuming helicopter transport can be arranged, said Depland.
"I would expect, assuming the storm goes according to our assumptions, we'll be making oil again tomorrow and probably be back mostly into production tomorrow," the spokesman said.
The hurricane shut in a number of fields and halted offloading of a crude shipment on Friday but onshore deliveries of crude oil continued unaffected, industry participants said.
